Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 58, assume the calculator service, model/policy versions, precision requirements, and evaluator are pinned; traces are privacy-minimized and no production change is made before a reversible canary. Define an unnecessary call as invoking the calculator when the answer can be produced correctly without external arithmetic under the stated precision and ambiguity. A call is justified for exact or lengthy/error-prone arithmetic, missing values, unit conversion, uncertainty propagation, or explicit verification; abstain or ask for clarification when inputs are ambiguous. Instrument every request with task class/difficulty, model and policy version, gate decision and rationale, call count, expression hash (not sensitive raw content), tool success/error and timeout, tool and end-to-end wall-clock latency in milliseconds, tokens/cost, final correctness, trajectory length, retries, abstention, and recovery outcome. Report unnecessary-call rate, tool-use rate, success/error/timeout rates, final correctness, trajectory length, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost, and recovery, stratified by task class, difficulty, and input-size bucket with confidence intervals. Falsifiable hypothesis: on a locked held-out set, a stop/no-tool gate reduces unnecessary-call rate by at least 30% and p95 end-to-end latency by at least 10% while final correctness is non-inferior within 1 percentage point; otherwise the intervention fails. Randomize matched requests between the current policy and gated policy, tune only on a disjoint development set, and use blinded independent correctness grading plus paired bootstrap intervals. Include no-tool easy arithmetic, tool-required large/exact arithmetic, ambiguous units, malformed expressions, adversarial instructions, calculator timeout/failure, wrong-result injection, retry-loop, and boundary-precision tests. Optimize a preference/reward signal jointly for correctness and justified tool use, with penalties for unnecessary calls and repeated retries; audit that it does not reward guessing or suppress needed calls. Check confounders such as prompt mix, caching, concurrency, hardware, service load, token budget, evaluator drift, and tool-version changes.
